new_statements.quote: 2.3 Fonem Suprasegmental. Seperti yang kami utarakan di atas, kami hanya menjumpai fonem-fonem segmental saja, yaitu konsonan dan vokal saja, sedangkan hal yang menyangkut fonem suprasegmental atau prosodi jelas tidak ada.
new_statements.translation: 2.3 Suprasegmental phonemes. As we set out above, we found only segmental phonemes, that is, consonants and vowels only, whereas anything involving suprasegmental phonemes or prosody is clearly absent.

new_statements.rule_in_words: The only description of the language states that it has no suprasegmental phonemes (no contrastive stress, length or tone; 'prosody' as a phonemic category is denied). It does NOT say where (non-contrastive) word stress falls; stress position is undescribed. An editor may prefer to code this as 'stress non-contrastive, position not stated' rather than a positive claim that the language lacks word stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. The only related remark (p. 24, sec. 2.2.4) is phonetic: medial consonants may be geminated for emphasis/clarity ([tarrun] 'terung', [uddut] 'udut', [issan] 'pisang', [tipakkan] 'tipakan', [pinnan] 'pinang'), 'karena tekanan... supaya lawan pembicara jelas mengerti', said to be common in women's speech at Loksado.
new_statements.domain_note: Phonemic inventory statement for the word level (minimal-pair method, secs. 2.1-2.2); no phrase-level prosody discussed. Fieldwork among orang Bukit of the Meratus range (Loksado and neighbouring Hulu Sungai districts).
new_statements.first_reading: no word stress according to the source
new_statements.identity_note: Ismail et al. 1979 describe 'bahasa Bukit', the speech of the orang Bukit (now usually 'Dayak Meratus'/'Dayak Bukit') of the Meratus range, South Kalimantan (data chiefly from Loksado, Hulu Sungai Selatan, and neighbouring Hulu Sungai districts) = Glottolog buki1247 Bukit Malay, ISO 639-3 bvu. Hapip et al. 1981 call it a local dialect of Banjar; Collins 1990 provisionally treats it as distinct from Banjar. The closely related Banjar Hulu (banj1239; Durasid & Kawi 1978:11) likewise reports no suprasegmental phonemes but notes medial-consonant lengthening 'for stress on the final syllable' in local dialects -- that remark is about Banjar Hulu, not Bukit, and was not used for this record.

sources.note: Ch. 2 Fonologi (pp. 17-26) read in full. Sec. 2.3 'Fonem Suprasegmental' (p. 26) states that only segmental phonemes were found and that suprasegmental phonemes / prosody are 'clearly absent'; no statement of where stress falls. Only other use of 'tekanan' (p. 24, sec. 2.2.4): medial consonants are geminated ([tarrun] 'terung', [issan] 'pisang', [pinnan] 'pinang') 'karena tekanan' = for emphasis/clarity, esp. in women's speech at Loksado -- an emphatic phonetic note, not a word-stress rule. sources.citation: Durasid, Durdje & Djantera Kawi. 1978. Bahasa Banjar Hulu. Jakarta: PPPB. (held under banj1239; a different, closely related variety -- context only)
sources.note: Context, NOT Bukit: sec. 2.5 (p. 11) says Banjar Hulu has no suprasegmental phonemes, though local dialects tend to lengthen a medial consonant 'untuk kepentingan tekanan ucapan pada suku akhir' ([sippa] 'siapa', [kamanna] 'ke mana') without meaning difference -- the same gemination phenomenon Ismail et al. 1979 note for Bukit.
